book.title: Liner Notes for the Revolution: The Intellectual Life of Black Feminist Sound

evidence: academic press signal: Harvard University Press / Harvard University Press
academic press signal: Harvard University Press / Harvard University Press

argument.statement: Overlooked contributions by Black women critics, collectors, and listeners provide new perspectives on how Black women musicians are perceived within the culture industry.

book.rationale: The book primarily engages with music criticism and cultural analysis through the lenses of race and gender, highlighting Black feminist perspectives on music and its impact.
book.summary: Winner of the Ralph J. Gleason Music Book Award, Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Winner of the American Book Award, Before Columbus Foundation Winner of the PEN Oakland–Josephine Miles Award Winner of the MAAH Stone Book Award A Pitchfork Best Music Book of the Year A Rolling Stone Best Music Book of the Year “Brooks traces all kinds of lines, finding unexpected points of connection...inviting voices to talk to one another, seeing what different perspectives can offer, opening up new ways of looking and listening by tracing lineages and calling for more space.” —New York Times An award-winning Black feminist music critic takes us on an epic journey through radical sound from Bessie Smith to Beyoncé. Daphne A. Brooks explores more than a century of music archives to examine the critics, collectors, and listeners who have determined perceptions of Black women on stage and in the recording studio. How is it possible, she asks, that iconic artists such as Aretha Franklin and Beyoncé exist simultaneously at the center and on the fringe of the culture industry? Liner Notes for the Revolution offers a startling new perspective on these acclaimed figures—a perspective informed by the overlooked contributions of other Black women concerned with the work of their musical peers.
